page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.3xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. Running on a KVM hypervisor, it provides 12 vCPUs mapped to 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance features a base CPU speed of 3.1 GHz, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 48.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.hfg6.3xlarge in the average performance tier across most categories. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance registers at 1438.78, while multi-core performance reaches 11511.8. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 642.07 GB/sec, dropping to 72.53 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and a write speed of 43.69 GB/sec. In application-specific tests, the instance achieves 11.25 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 10.16 GB/sec. For language model workloads, prompt processing with a small 135M model reaches 748.79 tokens per second, but performance drops significantly to a weak 17.47 tokens per second for a medium 7B model.

From a resource density perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offer a balanced hardware profile for general-purpose workloads. However, the lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment, which may impact overall I/O latency and cost. The 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth also presents a potential bottleneck for highly distributed systems. This instance is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, Redis caching, software compilation, and lightweight text or image processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.3xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose server instance featuring a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with 12 vCPUs, 6 physical cores, and a 3.1 GHz clock speed. It is configured with 48.0 GB of RAM, 35 MB of L3 cache, and a KVM hypervisor, but lacks local storage and has a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. Benchmark results indicate average performance across standard compute and memory tasks, with a single-core Geekbench score of 1290.0 and a multi-core score of 6470.0. It achieves 11.25 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 10.16 GB/sec in static web serving. The instance is suitable for general-purpose workloads, including web serving, caching, and software compilation, though it exhibits weak performance on larger language model inference tasks.
